# nish/net/http2-cleartext

HTTP/2 over plain TCP with prior knowledge (h2c, RFC 9113 §3.3): a pool of `Http2Connection`s, one per accepted socket, for a program that owns its readiness loop. The client starts with the 24-byte connection preface; there is no `Upgrade: h2c` (RFC 9113 §3.1 deprecates it) and no fallback to HTTP/1.1 on the same port.

```ts
import {
  H2C_DONE,
  H2C_POOL_FULL,
  H2C_WANT_READ,
  H2C_WANT_WRITE,
  Http2CleartextServer,
} from "nish/net/http2-cleartext";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { pollAdd, pollModify, tcpListen } from "nish:net";
import { H2_ERROR, H2_NEED_MORE, H2_REQUEST, Http2Config, Http2Connection } from "nish/net/http2";
import { H2C_DONE, Http2CleartextServer } from "nish/net/http2-cleartext";

// `loop` is the program's, from `pollCreate`.
const LISTENER: i32 = 64; // past every slot's token
const start = (loop: i32): Http2CleartextServer => {
  const listener: i32 = tcpListen("127.0.0.1", 8080, 128);
  pollAdd(loop, listener, 1, LISTENER);
  return new Http2CleartextServer(new Http2Config(), listener, 64, 10000);
};
// When the listener's token comes back:
const admit = (loop: i32, server: Http2CleartextServer): void => {
  const slot: i32 = server.accept();
  if (slot >= 0) { pollAdd(loop, server.fd(slot), 1, slot); }
};
// When a slot's token comes back with `events`:
const serve = (loop: i32, server: Http2CleartextServer, slot: i32, events: i32): void => {
  let wants: i32 = (events & 5) !== 0 ? server.readable(slot) : server.writable(slot);
  const none: u8[][] = [];
  let event: i32 = server.next(slot);
  while (event !== H2_NEED_MORE && event !== H2_ERROR) {
    const conn: Http2Connection = server.connection(slot);
    if (event === H2_REQUEST) { conn.respond(conn.stream, 200, none, none, true); }
    event = server.next(slot);
  }
  wants = server.flush(slot);
  if ((wants & H2C_DONE) !== 0) { server.close(slot); }
  else { pollModify(loop, server.fd(slot), wants & 3, slot); }
};
// Every so often, with `monotonicNanos()`:
//   server.expire(monotonicNanos());
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-detail title="No confidentiality, no integrity">

Anyone on the path reads and edits
the traffic. Serve h2c only upstream of a TLS-terminating proxy, on
loopback or a private network (`docs/security/http2-cleartext.md`).

</scalar-detail>

It is `nish/net/http2-tls`'s loop with a TCP socket in place of TLS, the
same method names and the same interest bits (read 1, write 2, done 16),
plus `expire(now)` for the preface deadline.

<scalar-detail title="The preface is the carrier's">

`Http2Connection` checks the preface
itself, but on a mismatch it queues SETTINGS and a GOAWAY, and a port
scanner or a confused HTTP/1.1 client should get nothing back. So each slot
reads its first 24 bytes into a 24-byte array of its own and compares each,
as it comes, with `PRI * HTTP/2.0\r\n\r\nSM\r\n\r\n`: at the first byte
that differs the socket is closed, with no byte sent. A whole preface is
fed to the connection, which checks it again, and from then on the socket
is read straight into the connection's input, as `http2-tls.ts` reads TLS
into it. Until the preface is whole the slot borrows no `Http2Pools`
buffer and sends nothing, so a peer that stalls there holds 24 bytes and a
slot until `expire` closes it, `prefaceTimeout` milliseconds after accept.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Relies on `@internal` members">

The carrier is the second server loop in
`std/net` and uses `Http2Connection.inputTail`, `received` and `endInput`
exactly as `http2-tls.ts` does. It keeps its own `ended` flag for the end of
input it passed to `endInput`, rather than reading the `@internal`
`inputEnded`.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-callout type="warning">

**Slots, a cap; buffers, borrowed.** As `Http2TlsServer`: slot 0's
connection is made by the constructor, so a bad `Http2Config` panics there
with its own words; every other slot's by the first `accept` into it, and
kept. Each connection borrows its frame buffers from the shared `pools`
and gives them back once empty and when the slot closes. Every final
response carries the pool's `date`, formatted at most once a second.

</scalar-callout>

Written from RFC 9113 §3, not ported from another implementation.

## Classes

### Http2CleartextServer

A pool of HTTP/2 connections over plain TCP, with prior knowledge, on one
listening socket. `connection(slot)` is the HTTP/2 side of each slot.

```ts
class Http2CleartextServer
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Http2CleartextServer(config: Http2Config, listener: i32, size: i32, prefaceTimeout: i32)` | A pool of `size` slots serving HTTP/2 under `config` on `listener`. Only slot 0's connection is made here, so a config it refuses panics now, with its words; every other slot's is made by the first `accept` into it and kept. The slots' preface arrays, 24 bytes each, are made here too. |
| `connections: Http2Connection[]` | The connections made so far, slot `k`'s at `k`: slot 0's, made by the constructor, and one for each slot accepted into since. |
| `date: HttpDate` | The `date` every slot's responses carry, formatted once a second for all of them: each slot's `Http2Connection.date` is its bytes, refreshed by `connection` and `next`. `date.pin` fixes its clock. |
| `readonly pools: Http2Pools` | The frame buffers every slot's connection borrows: one of each per slot at most, none made up front. |
| `accept(): i32` | Accepts the next waiting connection into a free slot and gives it a fresh HTTP/2 connection, which sends nothing until the peer's preface is whole: the slot's own, restarted, or one made now if this is the first accept into it. A slot closed before is taken first, then the next never used. |
| `busy(): i32` | How many slots hold a connection. |
| `close(slot: i32): void` | Ends `slot`'s connection and frees the slot at once: the socket is closed with nothing more sent, and the connection gives back every buffer it holds. |
| `connection(slot: i32): Http2Connection` | The HTTP/2 connection of `slot`, its `date` brought up to now. A slot never accepted into, or out of range, names slot 0's, which may be live. |
| `expire(now: i64): i32` | Closes every slot whose preface is not whole `prefaceTimeout` milliseconds after its accept, at `now`. A slot past its preface has no deadline here: a program times idle connections itself. |
| `fd(slot: i32): i32` | The descriptor of `slot`, for `pollAdd`. |
| `flush(slot: i32): i32` | Writes what `slot`'s connection holds to the socket, as far as the socket takes it, and answers the interest. Nothing is written while the preface is not whole. A socket that fails ends the connection. |
| `holds(slot: i32): boolean` | Whether `slot` holds a connection. |
| `next(slot: i32): i32` | Reads `slot`'s socket into its connection, as far as the connection has room, and answers the connection's next event. A slot whose preface is not whole reads that first and answers `H2_NEED_MORE` while it waits. |
| `prefaced(slot: i32): boolean` | Whether `slot` has read its whole connection preface, so its connection is running. |
| `readable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is readable: while the preface is not whole, reads it (and closes the slot at a byte that differs); then sends what HTTP/2 has to send. Once the preface is whole, `next` reads the socket. |
| `rest(slot: i32): void` | Gives back the buffers `slot`'s connection holds and has emptied, so an idle slot holds none. |
| `size(): i32` | How many slots the pool has, made or not. |
| `writable(slot: i32): i32` | The socket of `slot` is writable: what HTTP/2 holds goes out. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="16" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H2C_DONE: i32`

The interest bit for "the slot is over": the program calls `close(slot)`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-105" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H2C_POOL_FULL: i32`

What `accept` answers when every slot is busy; the connection it took is closed.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H2C_WANT_READ: i32`

The interest bit for "read the socket": `pollModify`'s read event.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`H2C_WANT_WRITE: i32`

The interest bit for "write the socket": `pollModify`'s write event.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
